description: Flat, translucent geometric primitives - triangles, squares and circles - stacked and rotated around a single centre on a near-black ground, in a tight palette of slate blue-grey, mid grey and off-white with one burnt-orange/ochre accent that appears in roughly half the twelve. I would call it 'layered vector rosettes' or 'translucent primitive mandalas': every token is a centred emblem floating in generous black margin, built by overlapping semi-transparent fills so the crossings read as lighter, cooler bands rather than by any line, texture, gradient or noise. The twelve share that construction absolutely - same alpha compositing, same palette, same centred radial/rotational placement - and differ mainly along three axes: which primitive dominates (a big right-pointing triangle, a flat disc, or a hexagonal cluster), how many satellites orbit it (from about four shapes to forty), and whether the orange is present. Density ranges from near-empty (9011, 10801: one dark triangle plus two pale ones) through calm inscribed figures (9906, 10085: a circle with a diamond or triangle inside it) to a dense six-point burst (9190, 9548) and one incoherent scatter of small squares with no centre at all (9727). The frame is used as a plain container and mostly respected with wide margins, but the busiest seeds (9190, 9548, 10980) run off the top and bottom edges and 10980's satellites fly out to the corners as disconnected debris. Across the three conditions the object keeps its identity and its palette while the satellite ring expands outward and grows, opacity and edge-lightness rise so the central mass looks more hollow or outlined, and everything rotates slightly - stress is the loosest, largest and palest state, recovery sits between stress and neutral and reads close to neutral.
seenAt120: Four or five silhouette families survive and little else: a grey right-pointing triangle (9011, 10622, 10801, and 10443's diamond reads as the same grey wedge), a plain grey disc (9369, 9906, 10085), an orange-and-grey starburst (9190, 10264, 10980) and one brown-and-grey lobed flower (9548), plus 9727 as unresolved grey confetti. Within each family the members are hard to tell apart - the four triangle seeds are near-interchangeable at this size. The orange accent is the single most legible identifier; the seeds without it collapse toward one dim grey shape, and 9369 in particular is so close in value to the black ground that it almost disappears.
